extracted.intended_audience: procurement attorneys, agency acquisition officials, federal employees/unions, and legal scholars
extracted.subtask_description: Identification and explanation of the legal and procedural standards governing Circular A-76 competitive sourcing studies, including how cost comparisons must be conducted and who has standing to protest those decisions at GAO and in court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apples-to-apples comparison requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The solicitation instructed the Source Selection Evaluation Team (SSET) to determine whether the MEO proposal represented a comparable level of performance to the selected contractor proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To ensure a fair cost comparison, the SSET must verify comparable performance levels between the MEO and contractor proposals; if not comparable, the SSA may direct the MEO to adjust its TPP or Management Plan. This 'apples-to-apples' leveling is required by the Supplemental Handbook and service regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: SSA authority to direct MEO adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Source Selection Authority (SSA) could direct the MEO to adjust its TPP (Total Personnel Plan) or Management Plan, or both, if found to be deficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the MEO does not represent a comparable level of performance, SSA-directed adjustments are permissible to achieve comparability before performing the cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leveling procedure per Supplemental Handbook/service regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: The solicitation and supplemental guidance require 'leveling' between contractor proposals and the MEO to enable meaningful cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leveling procedures (e.g., adjusting staffing, performance assumptions) must follow Supplemental Handbook and service-specific regulations (pt. I, ch. 3, para. H.3) to avoid biased comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost aggregation and comparison method
rubrics_metrics.description: When separate firms perform different function sets (e.g., BOS and airfield support), the total proposed price of the separate contractors is added and the sum compared against the MEO for all services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The evaluators must combine contractor proposed prices (including multiple firms if applicable) and compare the aggregate to the MEO estimate to determine relative cost-effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustments for contract administration and conversion costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost comparisons must include adjustments for contract administration and one-time conversion costs, and apply mandated conversion reductions to avoid outsourcing for marginal savings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the MEO cost estimate may be reduced by a minimum $10 million conversion reduction as required by the Supplemental Handbook (pt. I, ch. 4, para. A.1) to ensure the Government does not convert to contractor performance for marginal cost savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence and certification of cost-comparison signatory
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost comparison form must be certified by an individual organizationally independent of the function under study; certification by a non-independent person violates guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD IG criticized a case where the MEO study team leader (not independent of the function) signed to meet a deadline. IRO review must adequately address MEO sufficiency prior to MEO certification/submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient training, experience, and time for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent Review Officer (IRO), SSET, and AAP Review Team members must have adequate training, experience, and realistic time to perform their review functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD IG found failures where reviewers lacked training, experience, and time, leading to inadequate assessment of MEO sufficiency and flawed evaluations. Teams should be appropriately staffed and trained for complex A-76 studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational conflict of interest / participation restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel who have knowledge of figures in the Government cost estimate generally shall not participate in the offer-evaluation process unless the contract file documents that no other qualified personnel were available (FAR § 7.304(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid conflicts, agencies must document any exception showing lack of other qualified personnel; participation by involved individuals can compromise appearance of independence and impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: AAP Authority and review-team independence/seniority
rubrics_metrics.description: The AAP Authority should be independent of and senior to the SSA (e.g., from another major command) to avoid apparent conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD IG recommended the AAP Authority be from another command and senior in rank to the SSA; appointment of subordinate or non-independent authorities undermines the appearance and reality of impartial appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility to serve on appeals if previously involved
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons who had previous involvement in the A-76 cost comparison under review are ineligible to serve on an administrative appeal board (DoD Interim Guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisors and participants who cross the line by actively participating in review team meetings may compromise independence; the Interim Guidance excludes prior participants from appeal boards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of evaluation rationale and adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract files and evaluation records must document comparisons, leveling decisions, staffing adjustments, and the rationale for any changes to MEO or contractor figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD IG criticized insufficient documentation (e.g., SSET failing to compare MEO to contractor proposals as required). Proper documentation is necessary to justify adjustments and to withstand protests or audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit-agency review when many FTEs involved
rubrics_metrics.description: Under some service regulations (Army/Navy/Marine), review by the service audit agency is required when a study involves a significant number of FTE positions; Air Force practice should consider such audit review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AFAA (or service audit agency) review can identify unresolved issues that materially affect cost-comparison outcomes; lack of such review in large, complex competitions is risky.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of external/independent review and corrective options
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspector General or audit agency reviews may recommend corrective options including canceling the solicitation and reinitiating the competition; modifying solicitation/PWS; directing SSA to re-review staffing adjustments; or appointing a new AAP Authority/Review Team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD IG offered remedial options rather than mandatory actions; agencies frequently respond with internal rebuttals or further audits (e.g., AFAA) which may lead to cancellation and restart of competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: GAO 'interested party' standing definition (CICA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under CICA and GAO Bid Protest Regulations, an 'interested party' is an actual or prospective bidder or offeror whose direct economic interest would be affected by award or failure to award the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the MEO management plan is not submitted in response to a solicitation and no contract is awarded when in-house performance is selected, individuals associated with the MEO are not 'offerors' and thus generally lack standing at GAO.

rubrics_metrics.name: GAO scope for considering protests by private-sector offerors
rubrics_metrics.description: GAO will consider private-sector offeror protests alleging agency noncompliance with applicable procedures or evaluation inconsistent with solicitation criteria, or other unreasonableness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private bidders may protest A-76 competitions when they can show procedural defects or unreasonable evaluations relative to the solicitation criteria; GAO has repeatedly entertained such contractor protests.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAIR Act does not expand GAO standing beyond CICA
rubrics_metrics.description: GAO concluded that the FAIR Act's language equating agency employees and their representatives to 'actual or prospective offerors' was not intended to alter the CICA definition of 'interested party.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative history and statutory text do not provide GAO a basis to broaden standing for employees/unions under CICA; GAO has rejected arguments that FAIR Act changed this definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of non-statutory protests under 4 C.F.R. §21.13
rubrics_metrics.description: GAO can consider protests brought on non-statutory bases pursuant to 4 C.F.R. § 21.13 when the agency agrees in writing to such consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an agency consents in writing, GAO may entertain non-statutory protests by parties who otherwise lack CICA standing; absent such written agreement, GAO will dismiss employee/union protests.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAR definitions' effect on MEO treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Under FAR definitions of 'offer' and 'contract,' the MEO is not an 'offer' because it is not submitted in response to a solicitation that, if accepted, would bind the offeror to perform a contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because no conventional offeror/contract relationship exists for an MEO competing to keep work in-house, the MEO cannot be treated as an actual or prospective offeror for purposes of CICA standing analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective action guidance under GAO/FAR/AFFAR
rubrics_metrics.description: Under FAR § 33.102(b)(1) GAO encourages agencies to take corrective action when a protest has merit; AFFAR § 33.102 requires contracting officers to contact the protester, fully consider merits, and take appropriate action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When agencies determine protests have merit, they should pursue corrective actions (e.g., adjust comparisons, reduce fees) rather than defend flawed procedures; GAO may dismiss protests as academic if agency takes corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial standing trends for employees/unions
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal courts (including the Court of Federal Claims and district courts) have repeatedly dismissed Circular A-76 challenges by employees and unions for lack of standing; the Federal Circuit has affirmed this posture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because courts have interpreted relevant statutes and precedent narrowly, employees and unions generally cannot challenge A-76 competitive sourcing decisions in COFC or federal district courts absent a change in statutory law or controlling precedent.
